speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to begin the examination. Since this is a newborn with respiratory distress, I need to clarify your exact age in hours or days and ask if you noticed any cyanosis or grunting at birth. REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas and Pulse_Oximetry.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L; Pulse_Oximetry: Peripheral cyanosis observed.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth at 33 weeks of gestation. Social history: N/A

speaker: Patient
text: The newborn is showing signs of respiratory distress including increased respiratory rate, grunting, and retractions. No other system review was mentioned due to the age of the patient. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Pneumonia (likely Klebsiella pneumoniae, given the history of maternal TB exposure). Although the patient was referred with a suspicion of Tuberculosis, the acute onset of grunting, retractions, and respiratory distress in a newborn is most consistent with primary bacterial pneumonia. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
